traits.crown_see_through.note: Imagekit woody-forms photo measures (2026-10-19, plantgen-claude project-files/image-data/woody-forms-2026-10-19/CROWNS.md): median sky inside the crown outline of 2 side-view photographs of leafy open-grown trees, plantc measure-mask: 0.12.

traits.trunk_fork_height_m.note: The stem forks into its big limbs about 5 m up, read by eye against the trunk in iNaturalist photographs of open-grown trees (observations 28744863, 83148498).

traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.33, 0.32, 0.3], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leader.note: Imagekit woody-forms group 1 (2026-10-19, plantgen-claude project-files/image-data/woody-forms-2026-10-19/): a few tortuous scaffold limbs (2) in the photos where renders draw about 6 straight ones; Sargent (p. 296): 'stout ascending or spreading branches forming a broad compact head'.

traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 296): 'stout ascending or spreading branches forming a broad compact head'. Spreading, as open-grown trees in iNaturalist photographs (batch inat-2026-10-23, picks 21 and 68) hold their big limbs past half way to level; Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990, Stein, Quercus garryana) calls the old open-grown trees 'large spreading trees'. Was ascending until 2026-10-24.

traits.crown_spread.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990, Stein, Quercus garryana): an open-grown tree 8 m tall and 8 m in crown spread bore a fair acorn crop; the record tree is 36.6 m tall with a crown spread of 38.4 m (1.05); open-grown trees have 'dense, rounded crowns' on very large, crooked branches. So an open-grown Oregon white oak is about as wide as it is tall, where the genus value (0.92) is the Urban Tree Database's street oaks.

traits.limb_course.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990, Stein, Quercus garryana), Growth and Yield: 'Typically, open-grown trees have short boles bearing very large, crooked branches that form dense, rounded crowns'; forest-grown trees have 'slim, straight boles, fine side branches'.

traits.trunk_fork_stems.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990, Stein, Quercus garryana): open-grown trees' short boles bear 'very large, crooked branches'; counted on iNaturalist photographs of open-grown trees (batch inat-2026-10-23, picks 21 and 68; imagekit woody-forms group 1, 2026-10-19: a few scaffold limbs, 2): the trunk divides into two.

appearance.bark_look.stages.mature.colou.note: text: 'light gray or almost white' (FNA), 'light grayish-brown' (Sudworth)

traits.leaf_habit.note: Wikipedia, Quercus garryana (read 2026-10-18): "The leaves are deciduous".

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Quercus garryana (read 2026-10-18): "Its fall color is unspectacular, with many trees turning plain brown". Colour ours.

appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17), as Quercus Garryana: "stout branchlets coated at first with thick pale rufous pubescence, pubescent or tomentose and light or dark orange color during their first winter, becoming glabrous and rather bright reddish brown in their second year and ultimately gray". Colour chosen by eye between the pubescent orange and the reddish brown.

generator.params.spur_pairs.note: An oak's leaves crowd at its twig tips, where the internodes are short (University of Washington botany notes), and a short growth unit bears about 5 to 8 leaves (Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson 1978, the general figure for preformed short shoots); three pairs is six. With single leaves at their flora length (woody forms, 2026-10-17), two pairs left the open-grown crown at 2.0 m² of leaf per m² of crown, the bottom of the Urban Tree Database's valley oaks, where Karlik and McKay (2002) measured 4.4 under a blue oak's crown.

traits.crown_form.note: Open-grown trees in iNaturalist research-grade photographs (observations 28744863, 28832264, 83148498) spread wider than tall on a few big limbs that rise from a short trunk and arch outward.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS (Quercus garryana): April to June across the range; it gives no months for Washington, Oregon or British Columbia, and too few iNaturalist records in the Puget Sound lowlands are annotated as flowering to count (6).

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 26 plant-years at 17 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Jul 1, Aug 10, Sep 14, Oct 9, Nov 4); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, August to October. FEIS (Quercus garryana): acorns ripen from August to November across the range.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Quercus garryana: grows 15 m to 20 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Quercus garryana: leaves 10 cm to 15 cm long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Quercus garryana: petioles pubescent, 15-25 mm long.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Quercus garryana (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.65 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 5 records in 4 sources); trunks 0.65, branches 0.65. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Gucker 2007, read): trees less than 20 years old did not produce acorns, but production increased with age until trees were nearly 80 years old (epicormic branches bore acorns 5 years after sprouting). It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 20 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Its blooms are hand-set from general knowledge of the species. Its growth takes the broadleaf trees' rules throughout since 2026-10-28, where a hand-set free-space density, internode, shoot length, bud break, branch and leaf angles, apical control, lean, wiggle, droop and path_half (fitted to the height reference) made a short, sparse ball of tufts unlike its photographs. Its trunk is the pipe model's from its leaves, by the broadleaf trees' rules (2026-10-23). Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: The USDA Urban Tree Database's open-grown white oaks, as for its leaf area per crown area, since it has no Oregon white oaks: Sacramento's valley oaks (Quercus lobata) 60 to 100 years old, 14 trees, median 68 years, 17.5 m tall and 78 cm through. Silvics (vol. 2, 1990) gives mature Oregon white oaks 60 to 100 cm through, and open-grown ones short boles under wide crowns. Was 15 m and 50 cm at 80 years, from general knowledge (broadleaf revision 28).

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark, glossy green leaves; pale grey, furrowed bark carrying moss and lichen. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: green acorns about 2.5 cm long in shallow, scaly cups, singly or in pairs. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: catkins in April and May; acorns green in summer, ripe and falling in September and October. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): light grey bark, furrowed and checkered into scaly ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves of the outer crown small, narrow and deeply lobed, shade leaves inside it larger, broader and shallower, as in other oaks; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured. Leaf (plant roadmap P4): the lobes rounded (`round` 0.8), as Oregon white oak's are. Single leaves at their flora length since woody forms (2026-10-17), not sprigs, so `leaf_area` is the area the leaf draws.
